Fit regressions for one or more outcomes and collect publication-ready results

Source: R/clean_regress.R
clean_regress.Rd

Fits one model per dependent variable (linear, logistic, Poisson, negative binomial, or ordinal; each also as a mixed model or a Bayesian brms model), computes robust or model-based inference, keeps reference categories as explicit rows, optionally adds pairwise contrasts, and applies multiple-comparison corrections within factors and/or across outcomes. Render the result with cr_table() (or just print it in a Quarto chunk), save it with cr_save(), and cite numbers in text with cr_inline().

Usage

clean_regress(
  data,
  dvs,
  predictors = NULL,
  random = NULL,
  formulas = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  se = c("robust", "model"),
  contrasts = NULL,
  contrast_adjust = "holm",
  dv_adjust = "none",
  dv_adjust_terms = NULL,
  exponentiate = TRUE,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  labels = NULL,
  level_labels = NULL,
  dv_labels = NULL,
  clean_labels = TRUE,
  label_case = "sentence",
  intercept = TRUE,
  baseline = NULL,
  lin = NULL,
  contrast_by = NULL,
  fit_args = list()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

dvs

Named character vector mapping each outcome to a model type, e.g. c(trust = "linear", donated = "logistic", liking = "ordinal"). Types: "linear", "logistic", "poisson" (counts, or Poisson quasi-ML for skewed non-negative outcomes: ratio of means), "negbin" (overdispersed counts), "ordinal" (cumulative logit via ordinal::clm; "polr" is an alias, same model). Each becomes its mixed version when random is given (lmer, glmer, glmmTMB negative binomial, ordinal::clmm). Bayesian versions via brms: "bayes_linear", "bayes_logistic", "bayes_ordinal", "bayes_poisson", "bayes_negbin" (with or without random; pass priors, chains, iter, etc. in fit_args). An unnamed vector of outcome names is allowed when type is supplied.

predictors

One-sided formula (~ condition + age) or character vector of predictor terms shared by all outcomes.

random

Random-effects term(s) for mixed models, e.g. ~ (1 | id).

formulas

Optional named list of full formulas that override predictors/random for specific outcomes.

type

Model type used for every outcome when dvs is unnamed.

cluster

Column name to cluster robust SEs on. Defaults to the first grouping factor for mixed models and to none (HC3) for lm/logit.

se

"robust" (default; HC3, or CR2 when clustered or mixed) or "model".

contrasts

Pairwise contrasts: NULL (none), TRUE (every factor predictor with 3+ levels), or a character vector of factor names.

contrast_adjust

Correction across the pairwise contrasts of each factor (any emmeans adjust method: "holm", "tukey", "bonferroni", "fdr", "none", ...).

dv_adjust

Correction across outcomes, applied to each row separately (the same coefficient or contrast across all outcomes is one family). Any stats::p.adjust() method; "none" by default.

dv_adjust_terms

Variables whose rows get the across-outcome correction. NULL means every non-intercept row.

exponentiate

Report ratios: odds ratios (logistic), cumulative odds ratios (ordinal), incidence rate ratios (Poisson, negative binomial).

conf_level

Confidence level.

labels

Named vector of display labels for predictors, e.g. c(condition = "Framing condition"). Unlisted names are cleaned automatically (see clean_labels).

level_labels

Display labels for factor levels: a named vector applied to every factor (c(GainFraming = "Gain frame")) or a list per factor (list(condition = c(GainFraming = "Gain frame"))).

dv_labels

Named vector of display labels for outcomes.

clean_labels

Tidy names that have no explicit label: GainFraming -> "Gain framing", age_years -> "Age years". See clean_label().

label_case

Case for cleaned labels: "sentence", "title", or "asis".

intercept

Show the intercept row.

baseline

Pre-treatment measure of each outcome, added as a covariate centered on the analysis sample (ANCOVA): a named vector c(trust = "trust_pre"), or one column for every outcome.

lin

Treatment variable(s) to interact with the centered baseline (the Lin, 2013 estimator); treatment rows then estimate the effect at the mean baseline.

contrast_by

A moderator: pairwise contrasts are computed within each of its levels (simple effects), adjusted within each level.

fit_args

List of extra arguments passed to every model fitter, e.g. list(control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")).

Value

An object of class clean_results.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- clean_regress(
  d,
  dvs = c(trust = "linear", donated = "logistic"),
  predictors = ~ condition + age,
  random = ~ (1 | id),
  contrasts = "condition",
  dv_adjust = "holm"
)
res
cr_save(res, "tables/table2.docx")
} # }
